'''Myles Christian Turner''' (born March 24, 1996)<ref>{{cite web|title=Myles Turner Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/turnemy01.html|access-date=November 8, 2020|website=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref> is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played one season for the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]] before being selected by the [[Indiana Pacers]] with the 11th overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]]. Turner spent 10 seasons with the Pacers, reaching the [[2025 NBA Finals]] in his final year with the team. Standing at {{cvt|6|ft|11|in}}, Turner plays the [[center (basketball)|center]] position. He has [[List of NBA annual blocks leaders|led the league in blocks]] twice in his career.

==Early life==
Turner was born in [[Bedford, Texas]], to parents David Turner and Mary Turner, and started playing basketball at age 6.<ref name=twentyfourseven>{{cite web|last1=Helwagen|first1=Steven|title=Schools Turning Up Heat For Turner|url=https://247sports.com/Article/Schools-Turning-Up-Heat-For-Turner-156374|website=247sports.com|access-date=June 24, 2015|date=October 22, 2013}}</ref><ref name=usab>{{cite web|title=USA Basketball: Myles Turner|url=http://archive.usab.com/bios/turner_myles.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150624090508/http://archive.usab.com/bios/turner_myles.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 24, 2015|publisher=[[USA Basketball]]|access-date=June 23, 2015}}</ref> He attended [[List of schools of the Hurst-Euless-Bedford Independent School District#Junior high schools|Central Junior High School]], and as a {{convert|6|ft|2|in|m|adj=on}} freshman, he led his team to 28 wins.<ref name=dallasnews>{{cite web|last1=Smith|first1=Corbett|title=Euless Trinity's Myles Turner is nation's most sought-after recruit, yet late bloomer still developing|url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sports/high-schools/headlines/20140202-euless-trinity-s-myles-turner-most-sought-after-recruit-in-country-yet-still-developing.ece|website=dallasnews.com|publisher=[[Dallas Morning News]]|access-date=June 24, 2015|date=February 2, 2014}}</ref>

==High school career==
Throughout high school, Turner played [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] basketball for the Texas Select team during the springs and summers to further develop himself and gain recognition as a player, participating in well known tournaments and camps such as the LeBron camp, the Nike Big Man Skills Academy, the NBPA Top 100 camp, Adidas Nations, and the Elite 24 invitational.<ref name="dallasnews" /><ref name=cbsaau>{{cite web|last1=Borzello|first1=Jeff|title=Myles Turner stakes claim as biggest riser of the summer|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/22952279/myles-turner-stakes-claim-as-biggest-riser-of-the-summer|work=[[CBS Sports]]|access-date=June 24, 2015|date=July 31, 2013}}</ref>

Between his sophomore and junior year, Turner, then 6'7", [[ankle fracture|broke his ankle]] during the first spring game of AAU play, hurting his chances of [[Recruiting (college athletics)#College basketball|recruitment]], but soon recovered and gained some 30 pounds through two-a-day weight training regimen to improve his game.<ref name="dallasnews" /><ref name=espn>{{cite web|last1=Mecalf|first1=Myron|title=Being Texas' Myles Turner isn't easy|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/12305581/texas-freshman-myles-turner-learning-growing-amid-expectations-criticism|website=[[ESPN]]|access-date=June 24, 2015|date=March 8, 2015}}</ref>
 
In his junior year, after fully recovering, Turner averaged 15.7 points, 12.87 rebounds and 8.64 blocks per game, leading Trinity to a 17–13 record and reaching the state playoffs for the first time in 10 years, and only the ninth time in school history dating back to the school's establishment in 1968. He also accumulated six [[triple-double]]s.<ref name="twentyfourseven" />

During the 2013 AAU summer circuit, Turner maintained his high level of production, leading his Texas Select team to the title at the 2013 Jayhawk Invitational in front of coaches from most of the [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] schools.<ref name=prepforce>{{cite web|title=Myles Turner – The Rise Of A Star|url=http://www.prepforce.com/home/front-page/myles-turner-the-rise-of-a-star/|website=prepforce.com|access-date=June 24, 2015|date=August 5, 2013}}</ref><ref name=lawrence>{{cite news|last1=Bedore|first1=Gary|title=Texas prep Myles Turner turning heads|url=https://www2.ljworld.com/news/2013/apr/30/texas-prep-myles-turner-turning-heads/|access-date=June 24, 2015|work=[[Lawrence Journal-World]]|date=April 30, 2014}}</ref>

Going into his senior year, Turner began garnering nationwide attention and becoming a highly sought after recruit for his athleticism, ball handling, shooting ability, and natural shot blocking ability for someone of his height. He solidified that by finishing out his high school career with 18.1 points, 12.2 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 6.8 blocks per game, leading the Trojans to a 24–7 record.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Borzello|first1=Jeff|title=Breakdown: Top-five senior Myles Turner commits to Texas|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24546568/breakdown-top-five-senior-myles-turner-commits-to-texas|work=CBS Sports|access-date=June 24, 2015}}</ref>

After finishing off his senior year, Turner was one of the last highly sought after recruits left that were uncommitted. He was rated a five-star prospect by many sites including [[Rivals.com]] and several more [[college basketball]] analysts as well as being considered the No. 2 center in the nation behind [[Jahlil Okafor]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Myles Turner|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Myles-Turner-23970|website=247Sports.com|publisher=CBSSports.com|access-date=June 30, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Myles Turner|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Myles-Turner-134245|website=Yahoo! Sports|publisher=Rivals|access-date=June 30, 2014}}</ref> Originally going into his senior year in fall of 2013, Turner had already accumulated 60 offers,<ref name="cbsaau" /> but by his senior year, the list was narrowed down to [[University of Texas at Austin|Texas]], [[University of Kansas|Kansas]], [[Duke University|Duke]], [[University of Arizona|Arizona]], [[University of Kentucky|Kentucky]], [[Ohio State University|Ohio State]] and [[Oklahoma State University|Oklahoma State]].<ref name=br>{{cite web|last1=King|first1=Jason|title=King's Court: Top Unsigned Recruit Myles Turner Opens Up on College Options|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1957548-kings-court-top-unsigned-recruit-myles-turner-opens-up-on-college-options|website=bleacherreport.com|publisher=[[Bleacher Report]]|access-date=June 24, 2015|date=February 12, 2015}}</ref> On April 30, 2014, live on [[ESPNU]]'s ''[[ESPNU Recruiting Insider|Recruiting Insider]]'', Turner formally announced his commitment to play basketball for the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|University of Texas]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Biancardi|first1=Paul|title=Myles Turner chooses Texas|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/10862976/myles-turner-nation-no-2-recruit-play-texas-longhorns|website=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN|access-date=June 24, 2015|date=April 30, 2014}}</ref>

Turner took part in the [[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]], in which he recorded seven points and seven rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Zimmerman|first1=Kevin|title=2014 McDonald's All-American Game: Jahlil Okafor, Myles Turner lead rosters|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2014/1/29/5359172/2014-mcdonalds-all-american-game-jahlil-okafor|website=SBNation.com|date=January 29, 2014 |access-date=June 30, 2014}}</ref> He also represented the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States]] in the [[2014 FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]], helping the country win a gold medal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2014/06/mens-u18-national-team-claims-2014-fiba-americas-u18-championship-gold-with-victory-over-canada.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140722190230/http://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2014/06/mens-u18-national-team-claims-2014-fiba-americas-u18-championship-gold-with-victory-over-canada.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 22, 2014|title=Mens U18 National Team Claims 2014 FIBA Americas U18 Championship|website=USAB.com|date=June 24, 2014|access-date=January 2, 2022}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman at [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] in 2014–15, Turner averaged 10.1 points, 6.5 rebounds and 2.6 blocks per game, earning 2015 Big 12 Freshman of the Year honors.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://big12sports.com/news/2015/3/8/209934691.aspx|title=Sooners' Hield Leads All-Big 12 Men's Basketball Honors|website=Big12sports.com|access-date=November 22, 2021}}</ref>

On March 30, 2015, Turner declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final three years of college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2015/story/_/id/12586407/texas-longhorns-freshman-myles-turner-enter-nba-draft|title=Myles Turner to go pro|date=March 30, 2015|access-date=March 31, 2015|last1=Goodman|first1=Jeff|publisher=ESPN}}</ref> In June 2015, Turner said, "The decision wasn't really that hard because I knew I would be picked pretty high, so I knew this was my opportunity to go."<ref>{{cite news|last1=Dwain|first1=Price|title=Myles Turner's NBA dream will soon become reality|url=http://www.star-telegram.com/sports/nba/dallas-mavericks/article25367233.html|access-date=June 24, 2015|work=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]]|date=June 23, 2015}}</ref>

==Professional career==

=== Indiana Pacers (2015–2025) ===

Turner was selected by the [[Indiana Pacers]] with the 11th overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/pacers-add-turner-young-2015-draft|title=Pacers Add Turner, Young in 2015 Draft|date=June 26, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 26, 2015}}</ref> He missed 21 games between November 13 and December 28 of his rookie season after undergoing surgery to repair a fracture in his left thumb.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/news/sources--pacers-rookie-myles-turner-to-undergo-thumb-surgery-monday-181011440.html Sources: Pacers rookie Myles Turner to undergo thumb surgery Monday], Sports.yahoo.com</ref><ref>[https://www.nba.com/games/20151230/INDCHI/gameinfo.html Butler's tip-in gives Bulls 102-100 OT win over Pacers], Nba.com</ref> On January 22, 2016, he scored a then career-high 31 points in a 122–110 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160122/INDGSW/gameinfo.html |title=Curry's triple-double leads Warriors to win in Kerr's return |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=January 23, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160123033349/http://www.nba.com/games/20160122/INDGSW/gameinfo.html |archive-date=January 23, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On March 3, he was named Eastern Conference Rookie of the Month for February after ranking third among East first-year players in scoring (13.4 ppg), rebounding (6.6 rpg) and minutes (29.8 mpg) during the month.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/myles-turner-named-eastern-conference-rookie-month|title=Myles Turner Named Eastern Conference Rookie of the Month|website=Indiana Pacers|access-date=November 22, 2021}}</ref> On March 24, he recorded 24 points and a career-high 16 rebounds in a 92–84 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>[https://www.nba.com/games/20160324/NOPIND/gameinfo.html Pacers celebrate Turner's big birthday by beating Pelicans], Nba.com</ref> Turner helped the Pacers reach to the [[2016 NBA Playoffs|playoffs]] as the seventh seed in the Eastern Conference with a 45–37 record, where they lost 4–3 to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in the first round. At the season's end, he earned [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] honors.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2016/news/05/19/2015-16-all-rookie-first-and-second-teams-karl-anthony-towns-kristaps-porzingis-devin-booker-nikola-jokic-jahlil-okafor/|title=Wolves' Towns, Knicks' Porzingis lead 2015-16 NBA All-Rookie teams|work=NBA.com|date=May 19, 2016|access-date=May 19, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160522114420/http://www.nba.com/2016/news/05/19/2015-16-all-rookie-first-and-second-teams-karl-anthony-towns-kristaps-porzingis-devin-booker-nikola-jokic-jahlil-okafor|archive-date=May 22, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>[[File:Myles Turner dunk.jpg|thumb|Turner dunking for the Pacers in 2017]]
In the Pacers' season opener on October 26, 2016, Turner recorded 30 points and a career-high-tying 16 rebounds in a 130–121 overtime win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899379|title=Turner's opening act leads Pacers past Mavs, 130-121 in OT|work=ESPN.com|date=October 26, 2016|access-date=October 26, 2016}}</ref> On December 15, he scored 26 points in a 102–95 loss to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899827|title=Davis, Hield lift Pelicans past Pacers, 102-95|work=ESPN.com|date=December 15, 2016|access-date=March 5, 2019}}</ref> On March 26, he had 17 points and tied a career high with 16 rebounds in a 107–94 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900487|title=Turner leads Pacers to 107-94 victory over 76ers|work=ESPN.com|date=March 26, 2017|access-date=March 26, 2017}}</ref>

Prior to the start of the 2017–18 season, Turner was elected team captain.<ref name=pacers-nets>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974701|title=Revamped Pacers rely on new faces to cut down Nets 140-131|work=ESPN.com|date=October 18, 2017|access-date=October 18, 2017}}</ref> In the Pacers' season opener on October 18, 2017, Turner had 21 points and 14 rebounds in a 140–131 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref name="pacers-nets" /> He missed the next eight games due to a concussion.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974872|title=Redick's 3s, Simmons' triple-double lead 76ers over Pacers|work=ESPN.com|date=November 3, 2017|access-date=March 5, 2019|quote=Turner hadn't played since sustaining a concussion in Indiana's season-opening win against Brooklyn on Oct. 18.}}</ref> On November 19, he scored a season-high 25 points against [[Miami Heat]].<ref name=br1718>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/turnemy01/gamelog/2018/|title=Myles Turner 2017-18 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=March 5, 2019}}</ref> Turner missed nine games in January with an injured right elbow.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975471|title=Pacers use late-game magic to rally past Orlando 114-112|work=ESPN.com|date=January 27, 2018|access-date=January 28, 2018}}</ref> On March 13, he tied his season high with 25 points against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref name="br1718" />

On February 25, 2020, Turner recorded a career-high eight blocks in a 119–80 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/wireStory/sabonis-scores-21-points-lead-pacers-hornets-119-69219589|title=Sabonis scores 21 points to lead Pacers over Hornets, 119-80|website=ABC News|publisher=Associated Press|date=February 25, 2020|access-date=October 22, 2021}}</ref> On December 22, 2020, in the Pacers' season-opener, Turner matched a career-high eight blocks in a 121–107 win over the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/game/nyk-vs-ind-0022000011|title=Sabonis, Oladipo lead Pacers past Knicks on opening night|website=NBA.com|last=Marot|first=Michael|date=December 22, 2020|access-date=October 22, 2021}}</ref> On January 6, 2021, he recorded eight blocks again in a 114–107 win over the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2021/01/07/pacers-vs-rockets-myles-turners-value-increases-even-2-points/6577525002/|title=Insider: Myles Turner's paid $17.5 million, scored 2 points ... and was worth every dollar|website=IndyStar|last=Michael|first=J.|date=January 6, 2021|access-date=October 22, 2021}}</ref> Turner finished the season with a league-leading 3.4 blocks per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/upon-further-review-myles-turner-wins-blocked-shot-season-title|title=Upon further review, Myles Turner wins 2020-21 blocked-shot season title|website=NBA.com|publisher=Associated Press|date=May 18, 2021|access-date=October 22, 2021}}</ref>

from the three-point line.<ref>{{cite web|last=Warren|first=Brook|date=March 28, 2022|url=https://www.slamonline.com/nba/report-myles-turner-out-for-the-rest-of-the-season/|title=Report: Myles Turner Out For the Rest of the Season|website=Slam Online|access-date=April 15, 2022}}</ref>

On January 20, 2023, Turner signed a two-year, $43 million extension through the 2024–25 season, that also included a $17 million increase in his 2022–23 salary.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 18, 2023 |title=Pacers, Myles Turner reach 2-year, $60M extension, agent says |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/35546473/pacers-myles-turner-reach-2-year-60m-extension-agent-says |access-date=2026-05-03 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

On February 23, 2023, Turner tied a career-high 40 points on a career-high eight three-pointers made and also put up 10 rebounds in a 142–138 overtime loss to the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/pacers-news-myles-turners-epic-feat-never-before-seen-in-nba-history|title=Myles Turner’s drops unreal stat line vs. Celtics no center in NBA history has ever done|website=ClutchPoints|last=Yapkowitz|first=David|date=February 23, 2023|access-date=February 23, 2023}}</ref>

On March 22, 2024, in a 123–111 win against the [[Golden State Warriors]], Turner recorded five blocks en route to becoming the all-time blocks leader in Pacers franchise history with his 1,246th block, surpassing the previous record set by [[Jermaine O'Neal]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2024/03/23/myles-turner-sets-blocks-record-as-pacers-defense-shines-in-win/73076761007/|title=Insider: Myles Turner's blocks record part of a night to celebrate for Pacers’ defense|website=Indy Star|last=Dopirak|first=Dustin|date=March 23, 2024|access-date=March 24, 2024}}</ref>

In Turner's final season with the Pacers, he helped the Pacers reach the [[2025 NBA Finals]], where they lost to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in seven games.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bontemps|first=Tim|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45565932/thunder-overwhelm-pacers-game-7-franchise-first-title|title=Thunder take Game 7, cap historic season with first title|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=22 June 2025|access-date=26 October 2025}}</ref>

===Milwaukee Bucks (2025–present) ===
On July 7, 2025, Turner signed a four-year, $108.9 million contract with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-myles-turner|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Myles Turner|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Bucks, Myles Turner Finalize Four-Year Deal |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/07/bucks-myles-turner-agree-to-four-year-deal.html |access-date=July 8, 2025 |website=Hoops Rumors}}</ref> This ended Turner's 10 year union with the Pacers. In his Bucks debut on October 22, 2025, Turner put up 11 points, eight rebounds, five assists, and three blocks in a 133–120 win over the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/milwaukee-bucks/bucks-news-myles-turners-reaction-bucks-debut|title=Myles Turner’s heartfelt reaction to memorable Bucks debut|website=ClutchPoints|last=Bhatnagar|first=Rishabh|date=October 23, 2025|access-date=October 23, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/bucks-giannis-antetokounmpo-jokes-about-building-chemistry-with-myles-turner-six-months-ago-he-hated-me/|title=Bucks' Giannis Antetokounmpo jokes about building chemistry with Myles Turner: 'Six months ago, he hated me'|website=CBS Sports|last=Maloney|first=Jack|date=October 23, 2025|access-date=October 23, 2025}}></ref>
